name: 4643-batchdecode-dsv2lite-8gpu
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite, bf16, unquantized, ~31 GB, in the local HF cache.
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3 of one node, NV18 all-to-all NVLink.
parallelism: TP=8 with data-parallel attention (DP=8) and expert parallelism EP=8 over the DeepEP backend, on eight GPUs of one node: 8 local experts per rank, no PP, no external cache tier.
architecture: DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, 15.7B total / 2.4B active, bf16. 27 layers, 26 of them MoE, hidden 2048, 64 routed experts with 6 per token plus 2 shared, MLA attention with 16 heads.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=128, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 512 requests with a 3600 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, SINGLE TURN, no prefix and no shared structure: exactly 1000 prompt tokens in and 1000 tokens out, both fixed. temperature 0.0 and ignore_eos true, so every request generates its full length. Seed 42.
purpose: A long-form drafting assistant on a mixture-of-experts model, serving 128 concurrent 1000-token prompts across eight GPUs.
launch:
# sglang launch arguments for this item.

model-path: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
trust-remote-code: true

# `--enable-deepep-moe` sets ep_size = dp_size and the engine asserts `--enable-dp-attention`
# beside it, so neither of those two is a free choice. 64 routed experts / 8 = 8 per rank.
tp-size: 8
dp-size: 8
enable-dp-attention: true
enable-deepep-moe: true

# With data-parallel attention the engine divides this by dp_size: each of the eight schedulers
# logs max_running_requests=16, i.e. 128 resident across the node.
max-running-requests: 128

disable-radix-cache: true
mem-fraction-static: 0.9

# Decode is declared eager here. Do not enable graphs: it changes the machine being run.
disable-cuda-graph: true

stream-output: true
